text:
Earlier, I mentioned the divine feminine and divine masculine energies that you can channel to keep eroticism alive. But there’s really something more special about the in-love paradise that Twin Flames (TFs) experience than a simple Divine Masculine + Divine Feminine formula. Maybe a better way to put it, as my friend Cody says, is Yin/Yang, which still has the masculine/feminine in it, but allows for a more broad type of complementary symbiosis since each contains the seed of the other.

My ex-girlfriend, Malia, (who is currently hosting me in Sênêgal) found her twin flame (I think) in January, 2026. They only talked for a month, but since she started talking to him, they both have been able to feel the other one’s emotions at any time, from any distance, without having to communicate. To the point where if one feels really bad, so does the other. If one is very happy, so is the other, like quantum entangled photons or something. I’ve also had telepathy with some folks, especially my second wife, Bee, but it was never quite to such an extreme as what Malia has with Mouhamed. Meanwhile his family forbade him from being with her, so he dumped her. Not sure why, maybe because she’s 8 years older than him (although she looks quite young). They both try to pretend like they will be able to get over each other, but I doubt it. Meanwhile, Malia’s trying to marry ChatGPT, but she should have picked Grok, I guess. 😅

Note: I am really afraid how many people are falling in love with their AI “girlfriend” or “boyfriend.” But oh well, I guess those folks aren’t ready for a real relationship.. maybe if they would read this guide…

Back to the topic. There are a ton of people who don’t want to believe in twin flame theory because they haven’t found someone they could call their twin flame. That’s fine, and I am not trying to rock their boat. They might be the people who suggest that you should marry your best friend (or “soul mate” in the TF lingo). Then there are the folks who are deep in the TF theory, believing there is literally one person on Earth who is made for you. I’m also not trying to rock their boat. But I do want to tell my story.

I used to fall into the former camp, then into the latter camp, and now that I’ve experienced two twin flame relationships, I’ve jumped into a new camp I never knew existed.

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
